extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners referencing MPEP practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for issuing and responding to requirements for information under 37 CFR 1.105, and for preparing and using Patentability Reports during USPTO examination. Focused on examiner obligations, form/content of requirements, reply handling, and related administrative rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate basis for making a requirement for information
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 may be made when the application file or lack of relevant prior art found in the examiner’s search justifies asking the applicant if he or she has information reasonably necessary to the patentability determination or to the examination/treatment of matters in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be combined with the first action on the merits if that action includes at least one rejection; rarely appropriate to require information because of a lack of relevant prior art after the first action on the merits; not proper when no further action would be taken by the examiner (reasonable necessity implies further action). Requirements may be made in issued or abandoned applications only under limited circumstances (e.g., proceedings to revive, change inventorship, reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing constraints for making requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not appropriate to make a requirement for information based on lack of relevant prior art with a first-action allowance or Ex parte Quayle action; requirements after the first action are rare and should be justified by the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements should generally be non-final actions because applicant’s reply must be considered; requirements made when no further action would be taken are improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies must be complete and timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to requirements for information must be complete and filed within the time period set including any extensions; failure to reply within the set period will result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All replies should be checked for completeness; any incomplete reply can be completed within the original time period including extensions. Supplemental replies filed after expiration must comply with other rules for submissions of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of 37 CFR 1.105 requirements to duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of candor and good faith under 37 CFR 1.56 applies to replies to 1.105 requirements and requires submission of information reasonably and readily available; however, the materiality threshold for 1.56 is substantially higher than the reasonable-necessity threshold for 1.105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike 1.56, 1.105 does not require searching for unknown information; information that may not be material to patentability may nevertheless be required under 1.105 because it is necessary to obtain a complete record for determining patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a complete reply to a 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply is a reply to each enumerated requirement giving either the information required or a statement that the information is unknown and/or not readily available to the party from which it was requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant need not prove the information was not attainable, but must make a good faith attempt and reasonable inquiry. A statement that information is unknown or not readily obtainable will generally be sufficient unless it is clear the applicant did not understand the requirement or the reply is ambiguous when a more specific answer is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of incomplete replies
rubrics_metrics.description: An incomplete reply to a 1.105 requirement in a pending application or reexamination proceeding is handled as an amendment not fully responsive to a non-final office action (see 37 CFR 1.135(c) and MPEP § 714.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the reply is bona fide, form paragraph 7.95 may be used. A requirement under 1.105 is an Office action even absent an action on the merits. Examiner cannot grant extension if omission was deliberate or application is subject to a final Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for reply to 1.105 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies or failures to reply are governed by 37 CFR 1.135 and 1.136; requirements made without an action on the merits should set a shortened statutory period of two months for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may extend the time for reply up to six months under 1.136(a). Requirements sent with an office action get the same period as that action. A 1.105 requirement is an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 for patent term adjustment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowly specify and limit scope of requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information under 1.105 should be narrowly specified and limited in scope because it is a significant burden on both the applicant and the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only warranted where expected benefit from obtaining the information exceeds the burden of obtaining and considering it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and content of the requirement (identify rule and basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement must clearly indicate that it is being made under 37 CFR 1.105, state the basis for the requirement, and specify the information being required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements should specify particular art areas and particular claimed subject matter to avoid overbroad requests; indicate the form the required information is expected to take (citations/copies, identification of collections, answers to questions, etc.). Preferably prepared as a separate document (though the rule permits inclusion within an Office action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.105 — Requirement for Information, Heading
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.105 to begin any requirement under 37 CFR 1.105: it informs applicant and assignee they are required to provide information the examiner has determined is reasonably necessary to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be followed by explanation of why information is necessary; other form paragraphs (7.106–7.121) may be used as appropriate, and the requirement should conclude with 7.122–7.126 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.106 — Domain of Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Request information to extend the domain of search for prior art, identifying limited amounts of art available in certain classes/subclasses and the need for a broader range of art to establish the level of knowledge of those of ordinary skill in the claimed art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by form paragraphs 7.122–7.126 as appropriate; bracketed fields require insertion of class/subclass and description of the claimed art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.107 — Level of Skill and Knowledge in the Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Request information required to document the level of skill and knowledge in the art of the disclosed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.108 — Background Description
rubrics_metrics.description: Require information to complete the background description in the disclosure by documenting specified items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.109 — Products and Services Embodying Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Require identification of products and services embodying the disclosed subject matter and the properties of similar products/services found in the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.110 — Art Suggested as Relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Require entry into the record of art suggested by applicant as relevant to examination, identifying where in the application the suggestion appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate; bracketed field should describe where applicant suggested relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.111 — List of Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Request a list of keywords helpful in locating publications related to the disclosed art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.112 — Citations for Electronically Searchable Databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Request citations to electronically searchable databases or other indexed collections containing publications documenting knowledge within the disclosed art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.113 — Copy of Art Referred to in Disclosure but Not Submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Request copies of items of art referred to in the application file that were not previously submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126; bracketed field should describe where in the file the art is referred to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.114 — Copies of Publications Authored by Inventor(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require copies of publications authored or co-authored by any of the applicants that describe the disclosed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.116 — Art Relied Upon for Development of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Require title, citation and copy of each publication any applicant relied upon to develop the disclosed subject matter, with concise explanation of the reliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied on (not merely believed relevant); must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.117 — Art Relied Upon for Drafting Claimed Subject Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Require title, citation and copy of each publication relied upon to draft the claimed subject matter and concise explanation of reliance in distinguishing claimed subject matter from prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied on; preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.118 — Results of Applicant’s Prior Art Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a statement whether any prior art search was performed; if so, provide citations for each prior art collection searched and copies/citations of art considered material to demonstrating knowledge of person having ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate; bracketed field describes subject matter for which art was required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.119 — Names of Products or Services Incorporating Claimed Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Require names of any products or services that have incorporated the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.120 — Names of Products or Services Incorporating Disclosed Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Require names of any products or services incorporating the disclosed prior art, with bracket specifying attributes of prior art approximating the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126; use bracket to narrow focus of reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.121 — Details of Improvement Over the Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a statement of specific improvements of the claimed subject matter over the disclosed prior art and indicate specific claim elements that provide those improvements; for means/steps-plus-function claims, provide page/line numbers describing claimed structure/acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.122 — Submission of Only Pertinent Pages Where Document is Large
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow response to copy requests for large bound texts or articles (>50 pages) by providing only the pages that provide the indicated subject matter or material related to applicant’s disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and used at conclusion of any requirement accompanying an Office action; use 7.126 if mailed without other Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.123 — Waiver of Fee and Statement Requirements for Certain IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Waives the fee and certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 for documents submitted in reply to the requirement, but only for documents within scope of the requirement and included in applicant’s first complete communication responding to the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any supplemental replies after the first communication or information disclosures beyond the scope are subject to 1.97 fees and certification where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.124 — Contents of Good Faith Reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Reminds applicant the reply must be made with candor and good faith under 37 CFR 1.56; where applicant does not have or cannot readily obtain an item, a statement that it is unknown or cannot be readily obtained will be accepted as complete for that item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.125 or 7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.125 — Conclusion for Requirement That Accompanies Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: States the requirement is an attachment to the enclosed Office action and that a complete reply to the Office action must include a complete reply to the requirement; time for reply coincides with the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be used when requirement accompanies an Office action (use 7.126 if mailed alone).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.126 — Conclusion of Requirement Mailed Without Any Other Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: States the requirement is subject to 37 CFR 1.134, 1.135 and 1.136 and has a shortened statutory period (usually 2 months); extensions may be granted under 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and used where the requirement is mailed without any other Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.127 — Conclusion of Office Action That Includes Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates that the Office action has an attached requirement under 1.105 and that a complete reply to the Office action must include a complete reply to the attached requirement; time for reply coincides with Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should appear at the end of any Office action including an attached requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s obligation to consider applicant’s reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must consider information submitted with the applicant’s reply and apply it as deemed appropriate; identification of areas of search must be considered and examiner must indicate which areas were used or not used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications may be placed in file wrapper search notes or by notations on applicant’s reply with initials/date. Answers to queries must be considered and the record must indicate consideration (minimally 'Considered' with initials/date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of art submitted in response
rubrics_metrics.description: Art submitted in response to a 1.105 requirement must be considered at least to the same extent as art submitted with an IDS under 1.97/1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant provides a written list of citations, examiner must indicate which art has been considered and which has not, similarly to IDS practice. If no list provided, examiner need not prepare one unless relying on the art in a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of consideration — in-scope vs beyond-scope submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is never appropriate to refuse to consider information submitted in reply that is within the scope of the 1.105 requirement; information beyond the scope need not be considered unless submitted in conformity with 1.97/1.98 and MPEP § 609.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of a 1.105 requirement is measured by the plain meaning of the text of the requirement; therefore scope must be carefully specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to modify or withdraw a 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to the Director of the Technology Center to have a 1.105 requirement withdrawn or modified, or to have information submitted under 1.105 considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition is not a reply to the requirement; the time period to reply to the 1.105 requirement continues to run while a petition is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of 1.105 replies to Information Disclosure Statement rules (37 CFR 1.97/1.98)
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial reply responsive to a 1.105 requirement and submitted within the original time period does not have to satisfy fee/certification requirements of 1.97/1.98; applicant should list references on form PTO-1449 to have citations entered in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any subsequent replies beyond the initial communication and any submissions beyond the scope of the 1.105 requirement are subject to 1.97/1.98 fees and certification where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on making next office action final after applicant’s 1.105 reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may NOT make the next Office action relying on art submitted in reply to a 1.105 requirement final unless all instances of the application of such art are necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice distinguishes 1.105 reply handling from practice following IDS submissions under 1.97/1.98 and MPEP § 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Patentability Reports (P.R.) — when to request
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application properly assigned to one Technology Center contains one or more claims classifiable in other Technology Centers that are not divisible inter se, the application may be referred to other TC(s) for a Patentability Report on designated claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.R. practice is to be used only in extraordinary circumstances and only when primary examiners and TC Director approve; P.R. is signed by the primary examiner in the reporting TC and returned to the original TC for placement in the file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and nature of a Patentability Report
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patentability Report is a memorandum that includes citation of all pertinent references and a complete action on all claims involved; the field of search covered should be endorsed on the file wrapper by the reporting examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PR need not be typed if legible. The reporting examiner may state that final action is in order as to referred claims; PRs are returned and placed in the file wrapper until final disposition of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling disagreement on Patentability Report
rubrics_metrics.description: If the primary examiner does not agree with the PR or any portion, he/she may consult the reporting primary examiner; if no agreement, the primary examiner having jurisdiction need not rely on the PR and may make their own action on the referred claims and remove the PR from the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both primary examiners agree that a PR is necessary and TC Director approves, forward with memorandum and prepare PR; if appeal is taken where referred claims are examinable in reporting TC and application otherwise allowable, transfer for appeal only may be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of examination in P.R. cases
rubrics_metrics.description: If supervisory examiners cannot agree on the order of examination by their TCs, the supervisory examiner having jurisdiction will direct that a complete search be made of art relevant to his/her claims prior to referring the application for a P.R.; the referred TC will be advised of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a different sequence of search is expedient, the order should be modified accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting, recording, and credit for Patentability Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Forwarding an application for a PR is not treated as a transfer by the forwarding TC; upon completion and return, it is not counted as a receipt or action by transfer, though credit is given for time spent; date status is determined on the basis of dates in the TC of original jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reminders should be furnished to the TC making the PR to ensure orderly progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of duplicate prints of drawings for P.R. purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: In PR applications having drawings, the examiner of the assigned case will furnish the reporting TC with prints of drawing sheets applicable for interference search purposes; notation on the file wrapper may indicate this has been done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When PR-prosecuted application is passed for issue or abandoned, notify each TC that submitted a PR and have reporting examiners note date of allowance or abandonment on duplicate prints; prints may later be destroyed when of no value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on use of Patentability Reports — when not proper
rubrics_metrics.description: PR practice is not obligatory and should be used only where it will save total examiner time or improve action quality due to specialized knowledge; PR is not proper where claims are related as manufacturing process and product, product and process that merely makes the product, or combination distinguished solely by characteristics of a subcombination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where claims are directed to the same character of invention but differ only in scope, PR prosecution is never proper. PR permitted only with Director approval where it demonstrably saves total examiner time.
